risks.note: Land values in prime micro-markets (Mumbai, Bengaluru, NCR) have risen approximately 20-40% over the past three years, increasing project costs and pressuring developer margins.
risks.risk: Rising land acquisition costs in key metropolitan markets

risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices (steel fluctuating 15-25%, cement up ~8-12%) and labour costs (up ~8-10% annually) can reduce project margins by 100-200 basis points on a 5-7% cost increase, particularly for fixed-price projects.

Average project cycles for redevelopment run 5-8 years due to multiple approvals, tenant negotiations, regulatory clearances and rehabilitation obligations, increasing exposure to market cycles, cost inflation and policy changes — structurally relevant given the Company's redevelopment/SRA focus.
risks.risk: Long gestation periods in redevelopment and SRA projects

risks.note: Project approvals in metropolitan cities can take 12-24 months, with complex redevelopment projects taking even longer; delays can cause cost overruns, deferred revenue recognition and increased financing costs.

The sector is capital intensive and dependent on external funding; tightening lending norms and selective financing by banks/NBFCs may constrain funding for greenfield, redevelopment and stressed-asset projects, and higher borrowing costs may hurt profitability and viability.

Consolidation favours large, organised developers, driving up land acquisition and customer acquisition costs and pressuring pricing and margins; differentiation increasingly depends on execution capability, brand and financial strength.

Key challenges specific to redevelopment/SRA projects include obtaining consent from society members, rehabilitation and transit accommodation requirements, changes in redevelopment regulations, litigation and title-related issues, and extended execution timelines, which can cause delays and higher carrying costs.
